_about: Credit-card tap-to-ride in Tokyo (and Osaka Metro). Every rule here was read on the operator's own page on the 'checked' date; anything an official page did not say is left out. Re-check before 2027-03-25 (one year after the 11-operator mutual use began) or sooner if JR East announces support.
title: Can You Tap a Credit Card at Tokyo Train Gates? JR vs Subway (2026)
description: Tokyo Metro, Toei and nine other Kanto railways take contactless cards at the gate. JR East does not. Where your card works, and what to do if you can't exit.
h1: Can you tap a credit card at Tokyo train gates?
lead: Yes on the subways, no on JR. Here is where a contactless Visa, Mastercard or phone works, why a gate can refuse it, and what to do if you are stuck inside.
quick: Tokyo Metro, Toei Subway and nine other Kanto railways take a contactless credit, debit or prepaid card, or a phone with one in its wallet.
JR East does not. That includes the Yamanote Line, the Chuo Line and the Narita Express.
Tap in and out with the same card or phone. A different card, even the same card on your phone, does not count.
A JR Pass is for JR trains. Tokyo Metro and Toei are not on its list of covered lines.
A Suica or PASMO works on all of these, JR included.

stuck.title: Can't get out of the gate?
stuck.intro: Don't keep tapping other cards. The gate is looking for the trip you started.
steps: Look for the gate next to the station office window, or press the call button on the gate. Walk there instead of trying other gates.
Show the card or phone you entered with
Hold up the exact card or phone you tapped on the way in. A second card, or the same card on a different device, starts a new trip.
Tell the staff your boarding station. They will tell you what to pay and how. If the card trip no longer counts, Tokyo Metro asks for cash or another non-credit payment.
Keep any number they give you
Tokyo Metro may give you a reception number. Its FAQ explains how to follow up online.
phrases: I got on at ___ station with this card. The gate won't open.
このカードで ___ 駅から乗りました。改札が開きません。
どうやって精算すればいいですか？
I only have a credit card.
クレジットカードしか持っていません。
stuck.phrasesNote: Show the Japanese to the staff. Fill in your station name in English; staff will understand.

where.title: Where can I tap my credit card?
where.intro: The rules belong to the railway company, not the station. A big station like Shinjuku has gates from several companies side by side, and only some of them take cards.

rows.name: Tokyo Metro
notes: You cannot ride on through onto JR East, Saitama Rapid Railway or Toyo Rapid Railway lines with the card.
You cannot start a card trip at Nakano. If you get off there, the fare is settled at the staffed counter with the card you used.
Changing between Tokyo Metro and Toei on a card gets ¥70 off, as with other tickets.

rows.name: Toei Subway
rows.cardText: All four lines, all stations (since 23 Dec 2025)
notes: Asakusa, Mita, Shinjuku and Oedo lines.
Toei says some gates are handled at the staffed window instead.

rows.name: Nine other Kanto railways
rows.cardText: Odakyu, Odakyu Hakone, Keio, Keikyu, Sotetsu, Seibu, Tokyu, Tobu, Yokohama Minatomirai
notes: Since 25 March 2026 these work together with Tokyo Metro and Toei: 11 operators, 54 lines, 729 stations.
Some operators cover only some stations (Tokyo Metro names Odakyu Hakone, Seibu and Tobu). Check the operator before relying on it.

rows.name: JR East
notes: Not at the gates and not at ticket machines or ticket offices. This covers the Yamanote, Chuo and Keihin-Tohoku lines, the Narita Express and JR East Shinkansen.
Use a Suica, PASMO or other transport IC card, or buy a ticket.

rows.name: Osaka Metro
notes: Adult fare only. Use the dedicated reader at the gate.
Osaka Metro does not say how card trips onto other companies' lines work. Ask staff before riding through.

where.others: Other lines, such as Keisei, the Tokyo Monorail or the Rinkai Line, are not among the 11 operators. A few run their own card service (Yurikamome, for example), which does not join up with the others. When in doubt, use your Suica.

why.title: Why your card might not work
items: The company does not take cards
JR East gates have no card reader at all. If you are at a JR gate, you need an IC card or a ticket.
Your train ran on to another company

Many subway trains continue onto other lines without you changing trains. On Tokyo Metro, a card trip that runs on to JR East, Saitama Rapid Railway or Toyo Rapid no longer counts, and you pay separately.
The station or gate is excluded
You cannot start a Tokyo Metro card trip at Nakano. Toei says some of its gates are handled at the staffed window instead.
You tapped out with something else
Entry and exit must be the same card on the same device. A physical card and the same card in Apple Pay are two different things.
The card reader is a separate, dedicated pad, not the round IC-card target. Tap the one with the contactless symbol and wait for the beep.
why.fallback: If none of these fits, go to the staffed gate. Staff can see what the gate recorded.

compare.title: Suica vs credit card vs JR Pass
compare.intro: For trains around a city, a transport IC card is still the simplest choice. A credit card is a good backup on the subway. The JR Pass is a different decision about long JR trips.

cards.name: Suica / PASMO (IC card)
points: Works on JR East, Tokyo Metro, Toei and the private railways.
One of ten IC cards that also work in other regions, such as ICOCA in Kansai.
PASMO can be added to the Wallet app on an iPhone 8 or later.

cards.name: Contactless credit card
points: No card to buy or top up. On Tokyo Metro, the same fare as a paper ticket.
Adult fare only, and not on JR East.
Tap in and out with the same card or phone.

cards.name: JR Pass
points: Covers JR trains and the Tokyo Monorail, but not Nozomi or Mizuho Shinkansen.
Tokyo Metro and Toei are not on its list. Don't buy it for subway rides.
Worth comparing only if your trip is built around long JR journeys.

subwayTicket.title: Riding the subway all day? Tokyo Subway Ticket
subwayTicket.text: Unlimited Tokyo Metro and Toei rides for 24, 48 or 72 hours: ¥1,000, ¥1,500 or ¥2,000 for adults. Sold to overseas visitors and to Japan residents from outside Tokyo and seven nearby prefectures. It does not cover JR.

faq: Can I use Apple Pay or Google Pay on the Tokyo subway?
Yes, if the phone has an eligible card in its wallet. Tokyo Metro accepts phones with Visa, Mastercard, JCB, American Express or Discover. Use the same phone to tap in and out.
Can I tap my credit card on the JR Yamanote Line?
No. JR East does not accept contactless credit cards at gates, ticket machines or ticket offices. Use a Suica or PASMO, or buy a ticket.
Can I tap a credit card at Shinjuku Station?
At the Tokyo Metro, Toei, Odakyu and Keio gates, yes. At the JR gates, no. Check which company's gate you are walking through.
Which cards does Tokyo Metro accept?
Visa, Mastercard, JCB, American Express, Diners Club, Discover and UnionPay cards with the tap-to-pay symbol: credit, debit or prepaid.
Do kids pay less with a credit card?
No. Card trips are charged the adult fare. Children should use a child IC card or a child ticket.
Can I take the Narita Express with a credit card tap?
No. The Narita Express is JR East. Buy a ticket or use a Suica.
Do I still need a Suica?
If you will ride any JR line, yes, or buy tickets for those trips. If you only ride the subway, a contactless card can be enough.
Does the JR Pass work on Tokyo Metro?
No. The JR Pass covers JR lines and the Tokyo Monorail. Tokyo Metro and Toei are not on its list of covered lines.
